claims.claim: Bunge's expanded post-Viterra network connects origination, storage, processing and merchandising across agricultural flows; structural value comes from routing optionality and asset density rather than control of an irreplaceable commodity bottleneck.

The successor bottleneck is integration quality and network utilization: broader physical reach improves resilience only if synergies, working-capital discipline and normalized returns exceed the added complexity and capital burden.

risks.risk: Processing and merchandising capacity is substitutable across global agribusiness peers; network breadth does not guarantee durable scarcity rents.
Climate, crop, trade-policy and crush-margin changes can move the economic bottleneck away from Bunge-controlled assets.

unknowns.unknown: Normalized post-Viterra return on the expanded asset base and durable synergy realization remain unproven across cycles.

claims.claim: Raised 2026 guidance and stronger Q2 adjusted EPS support current execution, but neither demonstrates normalized integration returns; commodity curves, crush margins, crop availability and policy can overwhelm company-specific execution.

The Viterra combination increases scale and routing options while also increasing integration, leverage and capital-allocation complexity; this is a resilience tradeoff rather than a present contradiction.

risks.risk: Commodity-margin cyclicality can make short-period earnings improvement a weak proxy for durable economics.
Integration costs, leverage trajectory and synergy capture can dilute the strategic value of greater scale.

unknowns.unknown: Multi-cycle synergy realization, leverage normalization and return on incremental invested capital require continued evidence.
